title: Thatched roof of straw or water reed
purpose: Generate tileable PBR maps of a thatched roof: overlapping courses of long straw laid down the slope or combed water reed showing its cut butts, with ragged course edges, weathering to grey and moss in the shelter of the courses. Use for cottage roofs, huts, barns and fantasy villages.

contract.signature: generate(width=256, height=256, seed=0, preset="default", directx_normal=False, **parameters) -> {map name: {"channels", "colour_space", "pixels"}}
contract.command_line: python straw_thatch.py --size 1024 --seed 7 --preset NAME --out DIR [--width W --height H] [--set NAME=VALUE] [--directx-normal] [--orm]

parameters.name: style
parameters.meaning: 0 long straw laid along the slope, 1 combed water reed showing the cut butts.

parameters.name: courses
parameters.meaning: Courses down the tile; each overlaps the one below.

parameters.name: density
parameters.meaning: Strands per course; 1 covers each course about three times over, so little shadow shows.

parameters.name: strand_width
parameters.meaning: Straw or reed thickness in texture units.

parameters.name: raggedness
parameters.meaning: How uneven the lower edge of each course is.

parameters.name: weathering
parameters.meaning: Greying of the straw with age.

parameters.name: moss
parameters.meaning: Moss in the shelter below each course edge.

parameters.name: hue_shift
parameters.meaning: Hue rotation of the albedo in turns.

presets.name: default
presets.description: Golden long-straw thatch with ragged course edges.

presets.name: water_reed
presets.description: Combed water reed: dense cut butts, crisp courses.

presets.name: weathered_grey
presets.description: Old grey thatch with moss under the course edges.

presets.name: fresh_wheat
presets.description: New pale wheat straw, fine and even.

limits: Courses are straight horizontal bands of painted strokes; ridges, eaves, gables and decorative ridge patterns are out of scope. The slope runs down the tile (ridge at the top), so map V along the roof slope. Strands are straight capsules with a z-buffer, not bent fibres, and the moss is a tint with a slight lift, not modelled growth. Strand counts are fixed per course, so very thin strands at small sizes are drawn at least about a pixel wide. Occlusion is a blurred-height estimate.
technique_references: Course bands with whole counts down the tile
Z-buffered capsule painting of strands with wrap-around
Height rising from the hidden top of a course to its exposed edge
Ragged course edges from random strand lengths
Noise-driven weathering and sheltered moss masks
Height to tangent-space normal by central differences
